title.en: GoSleep — global audit of the orchestration system

subtitle.en: Seven independent audits, synthesised against the owner's original mandate

audit.synthesizer.en: lead architect of shift 73 (Opus 5), read-only mode

audit.sources[5].zone.en: the five skills, judged as a product

audit.sources[7].note.en: 9 downgrades, 0 upgrades; all four CRITICAL labels removed

audit.sources[8].note.en: 15 downgrades, 1 upgrade; of five CRITICAL labels, not one survived

audit.caveats[0].en: EVERY finding has been calibrated: three independent red teams covered all seven domain reports. No zone was left unchecked.

audit.caveats[1].en: The result of three calibrations: THIRTEEN CRITICAL labels, not one of which survived; roughly thirty severity downgrades against two upgrades. The facts on this dashboard are reliable; the original judgements about their consequences were not.

audit.caveats[2].en: The red team named the cause of the bias: the framing “the owner doubts the readiness claims” was read as “hunt for the worst case” rather than “check harder in both directions”.

audit.caveats[3].en: The synthesiser withdrew FOUR of its own first-draft conclusions: two CRITICAL labels, “the web is a display case rather than a console” (an entire plan step rested on it), “five places where the skill contradicts the owner's orders”, and “RUNWAY is missing two inputs”.

audit.caveats[4].en: Three findings collapsed entirely as defects and moved to the withdrawn section: the web being read-only, the pulse cadence, and the supposed ban on reading a transcript.

audit.caveats[5].en: There is no long-term observation history: the heartbeat truncates itself to 200 lines, so all the empirical data here covers 2026-07-20 → 2026-07-24 only.

audit.caveats[6].en: Skills outside the audited five (agentic-report-creator, verifier-skeptic, remote-control, writing-prds) were not properly audited by anyone — a visible blind spot of this whole pass.

headline.one_liner.en: As a research and documentation project: 70–75 percent. As the product “the owner goes to sleep and the system delivers”: about 45. That figure was raised from 35 after three rounds of calibration — four of the synthesiser's own conclusions failed review, and what has been built turned out to be better than the first pass claimed. What holds it below half are three things no calibration changes: the watchdog is not armed, recurring work has nobody to run it, and a night has never once been worked.

headline.hardest_fact.en: The system has never once worked through a night. The record for continuous operation without turning to a human is 6 hours 47 minutes — and that was an evening that ran past midnight, with the owner awake. Across seven days of logs, the hours between 3 and 6 a.m. contain 18 events.

headline.note_on_counts.en: ZERO findings remain at CRITICAL after three calibrations. Thirteen CRITICAL labels were filed in total (six in the first wave, four in the web audit, five in the skills audit) — not one survived. Three findings collapsed completely as defects (severity WITHDRAWN). One was fixed during the audit itself (RESOLVED).

headline.top_actions[0].en: One hour of work: four surgical edits to the orchestrator's instructions (the roll trigger, a gate on the Workflow tool, how agents are actually started, the ban on git stash) plus the rule that editing those instructions is part of closing a shift.

headline.top_actions[1].en: One evening of hygiene: archive statuses, the cumulative figure on Cost, the glob depth of both shelves (today it hides this entire audit), and the number corrections in STATE.

headline.top_actions[2].en: One engine for everything that has to happen regularly — and the trigger for it was already designed in the original research; it simply fell out during implementation.

headline.top_actions[3].en: The web console: freshness, connectedness and the quality of a FIRST version. Acting from the web is not a defect — it is a deliberately deferred v2 and a question for you.

headline.product_gloss.en: Every mechanism that is meant to run without a human is either not switched on, or lives inside the LLM's own pulse.

headline.research_gloss.en: The research is deep and honest and the reports are self-contained. Their weak point is that they do not know what today looks like.

flagship_metric.name.en: How much of what was built is armed

flagship_metric.rationale.en: Not “how much have we built” but how much of what we built actually runs on this machine. Today that is zero — and this gap between the quality of the artefact and the working of the product is what the entire audit is about.

already_done[0].what.en: The audit's evidence base has been saved into git

already_done[0].evidence.en: Epic GSL-169 closed, PR #173 open; nine audit files, the owner's mandate and the question archive now live in docs/reports/system-audit-2026-07-24/evidence/

root_causes_note.en: The first draft had six root causes. The sixth (“the web is a display case, not a console”) was REMOVED by calibration: an interactive web console is deferred in the PRD as a deliberate decision, not missing as a defect.

root_causes[R1].title.en: The mechanisms we describe have nobody to run them

root_causes[R1].what.en: The project has learned to describe mechanisms precisely and test them honestly, but never set up a process that RUNS them. The runner turns out, every single time, to be a live orchestrator on its pulse — or an agent who happens to remember.

root_causes[R1].cure.en: One machine tick outside the LLM, plus the RESTORED debounce hook that was already designed. A calibration refinement that makes the cure cheaper: the trigger was designed and simply fell out during implementation — the original research, 05-lab-ui-mobile-autonomy.md:184, calls for literally “a PostToolUse async hook debounced on writes to docs/lab/”, and a PostToolUse hook is already installed in three places.

root_causes[R2].title.en: Acceptance checks the artefact, not whether it is armed

root_causes[R2].what.en: “Done” means “the code is written and the tests are green”. No acceptance review has ever asked whether the thing runs on THIS machine right now.

root_causes[R2].cure.en: An armed-check as a precondition for accepting a phase, and as a tile on Overview. A correction on who owes what: in the watchdog's case the outstanding step is addressed to YOU (runbook GSL-57) — but the root cause does not disappear, because acceptance still fails to distinguish “the code is ready” from “the mechanism is armed”.

root_causes[R3].title.en: The only witness to the system's liveness is the LLM's own self-report

root_causes[R3].what.en: The orchestrator's health is judged from fields it writes about itself: context_pct, cycle, open_workers, the name of its pane.

root_causes[R3].cure.en: Make the source of truth the machine-computed status from claude agents --json; add a progress signal — “cycle has not moved for N ticks” (this costs zero tokens); resolve the skill's internal 965/771 contradiction and document the telemetry method. REMOVED from this root cause: “telemetry is physically unavailable” — the ban on reading a transcript is addressed to the orchestrator regarding a worker's transcript, and the method is permitted and used daily.

root_causes[R4].title.en: The main indicator stays silent for want of a single missing number

root_causes[R4].what.en: The formulas are written correctly and honestly, and still cannot answer.

root_causes[R4].cure.en: One number from you — GOSLEEP_TOKEN_CEILING. A SUBSTANTIVE correction: ONE input is missing, not two; the “work” axis is declared on_exhaustion:completes and by construction does not affect the answer. And the absence of a ceiling is a state your own manifest explicitly provides for, in section 5.

root_causes[R5].title.en: Claims about the system have no owner responsible for updating them

root_causes[R5].what.en: There is no rule requiring a document that makes claims about the system to carry a date and the name of whoever keeps it current. The most expensive instance is the skills themselves: the loop “lesson → task → edit → commit” ran for 30 days and 37 commits, stopped on 10 July, and editing the authoritative copy is now nobody's job, because that copy sits outside git, outside Jira and outside review.

root_causes[R5].cure.en: Make editing the authoritative copy a mandatory item when closing a shift, exactly like the handoff, and give it a home in git. Add a “data correct as of” header to every document that makes claims. This is the root cause that survived calibration completely, and the red team called it the most valuable conclusion in the skills file.
